axes.model_access:
**The provider list is explicit, type-safe config classes, covering both cloud and local paths.**

Official `beta/model_configuration` page wording:

"The AG2 framework provides an explicit, predictable, and **type-safe** way to configure Large Language Models"

One Config class + one extra per provider:

- `OpenAIConfig` / `OpenAIResponsesConfig` (`ag2[openai]`)
- `AnthropicConfig` (`ag2[anthropic]`)
- `GeminiConfig` / `VertexAIConfig` (`ag2[gemini]`)
- `BedrockConfig` (`ag2[bedrock]`)
- `OllamaConfig` (`ag2[ollama]`)
- `DashScopeConfig` (`ag2[dashscope]`)
- `XAIConfig` (`ag2[xai]`)
- `ZAIConfig` (`ag2[zai]`)

**Local / self-hosted support is explicit.**

The official docs have a dedicated section "Self-Hosted and OpenAI-Compatible Models (vLLM, LM Studio, etc.)",
via `OpenAIConfig`'s base_url. The README also lists `ag2[ollama]`.

**Bedrock switched to the native async client** aiobotocore in v1.1.1. The official release marks it breaking.

**Unknown** — how tool calling / structured output reliability compares across providers, not stated officially
(`beta/model_configuration` and the Grok compatibility page checked).
axes.runtime:
**A pure Python library, async throughout, no hosted service.**

README wording:

"AG2 requires **Python version >= 3.10**"

"AG2 is **async throughout**. `Agent.ask(...)` starts a turn and returns an `AgentReply`"

Install is `pip install ag2[openai]`.

**The official docs give two scheduling links for multi-agent form** (`network/overview` page):

- default **`LocalLink`** — official description:

  "same-process duplex queues"

  i.e. hub + agents inside one process.

- switch to **`WsLink`** — official description:

  "the hub and each agent as separate OS processes connected over WebSocket"

  i.e. the hub and each agent live in separate OS processes.

When switching links the `HubClient` API is unchanged; no business-code changes needed.

**It does not operate an agent loop.**

Everything in the library runs on your own process / host; the official docs offer no hosted offering.
axes.local_files:
**The framework ships no general-purpose file tools. File capability comes from KnowledgeStore and the sandboxed shell tool.**

The latter's boundaries are written more clearly than most peers — the single most notable thing about this object.

**① Disk knowledge store.**

The official harness example uses `DiskKnowledgeStore(Path("./knowledge_demo"))`, official comment:

"Disk-backed, so anything the agent remembers **survives the process exiting**"

i.e. where knowledge lands on disk is decided by the directory you specify.

**② Restricted shell** (verified, see official release v1.1.1).

Restricted mode "runs commands **without a shell**".

When `SandboxShellTool` / `ShellAdapter` gets `allowed=[...]` or `readonly=True`,
it splits the command into argv. Then **it checks only the argv and executes it verbatim**:

**Official wording**: "Nothing can expand after the check"

Pipes / redirection / wildcards / variables are rejected in restricted mode.

- `readonly=True` allows only non-writing commands that launch no other programs
- `blocked=[...]` officially stated plainly:

  "remains **best-effort**. It is **not** a security boundary."

**Unknown** — framework-level default file-access boundaries and container-level isolation, not stated officially
(`network/overview`, `agent_harness` and the release page checked).
axes.background:
**"Still running after shutdown" is pure-library form on this site — there is no hosted background.**

But the durable messaging mechanism has an explicit official implementation. The Network capabilities listed on the `network/overview` page include:

"**Durable messaging** with replayable channel transcripts (**write-ahead log**)"

"**Distributed / cross-process deployment**: replace `LocalLink` with **`WsLink`**"

The hub holds authoritative state: registry, audit log, channel table, write-ahead logs. Clients are:

"thin frontends"

There is also a dedicated **Distributed Deployment** page.

It covers WsLink, serve_ws, auth, **at-least-once delivery**, reconnect and **task durability**.

**Long-term memory can survive across processes.** DiskKnowledgeStore persists to disk, see the local_files axis.

**But there is no vendor-hosted offering at all.**

Processes must run on your own servers; a true background needs your own containers / K8s.

**Unknown** — hosting options and the exact semantics of resume-after-crash, not stated officially
(`network/overview` page checked).
axes.tools:
**Tools, MCP and AG-UI are all verifiable from official sources; A2A is only seen in repository topics.**

**① Native tools.**

A plain Python function with the `@tool` decorator becomes a tool. Official wording:

"AG2 runs the **full tool-calling loop**: the model decides when to call it, AG2 executes it, and the result is fed back"

Agents can also be used as tools by other agents via `Agent.as_tool()`.

**② MCP.**

Official releases record ongoing maintenance of `MCPToolkit` and `MCPServerTool`:

- v1.1.1 "send exactly one `Authorization` header on every provider"
- v1.1.2 "fix(mcp): derive model output schemas from serialization"

**③ AG-UI.**

- v1.1.2 "feat(ag-ui)!: **serve AG-UI 1.0**"
- v1.1.1 supports "**Human input over AG-UI**" (questions via `context.input()` inside tools are raised as interrupts to the AG-UI client)

**④ Skills.**

Official releases contain skill-related fixes:

- "check local skill ownership before validating arguments"
- "execute nested scripts from declared paths"

**A2A can currently only be seen in the official repository topics (including `a2a`).**

This pass did not capture the body of a v1.0 A2A dedicated page, so it is not expanded.

Subtask delegation has separately auto-injected `run_subtask` / `run_subtasks` tools (see the context axis).
axes.context:
**This is the AG2 design that best matches this site's "state ≠ context" stance.**

It explicitly splits the harness into three groups of opt-in primitives.

Official `agent_harness` page wording:

"A bare `Agent` is just a model loop. The **harness** is the set of **opt-in primitives** you compose onto it"

Three key parameters:

- **`assembly=` (context policy)** — official examples include `WorkingMemoryPolicy` (injects `memory/working.md`
  into the system prompt), `SlidingWindowPolicy(max_events=50)` (caps history usage), `AlertPolicy`

- **`knowledge=`** — `KnowledgeConfig(store=..., compact=..., compact_trigger=..., aggregate=...)`,
  with `SummarizeCompact` / `TailWindowCompact` doing **context compaction** (README example "18 -> 3 events");
  `write_event_log` dumps stream history to `/log/{stream_id}.jsonl`

- **`tasks=` (off by default)** — when enabled, subtask tools are auto-injected; sub-Agents inherit parent tools by default,
  and **subtasks themselves have `tasks=False`**, official wording:

  **Official wording**: "recursive delegation is structurally impossible"

**The boundary is clear**: `compact=` governs window compaction.

`KnowledgeStore` governs cross-process persistent memory — the official docs describe the two separately.
axes.permissions:
**The official mechanisms come in two layers: HITL human review + restricted shell tools. Neither layer equals a container sandbox.**

**① HITL.**

README wording:

- calling `context.input(...)` inside a tool pauses the run to ask a human
- `hitl_hook` decides where the answer comes from (CLI / web UI / queue)

**② Tool approval.**

Release v1.1.1 states plainly:

"**Approval grants are keyed by tool implementation**"

and only one same-named tool is exposed per turn.

MCP-discovered tools rank below code-declared tools and cannot override local tools.

**③ Restricted shell.**

`SandboxShellTool`'s `allowed` / `readonly` / `blocked` — see the local_files axis.
The official docs themselves declare `blocked=[...]` **not a security boundary**.

v1.1.2 also fixed a shell command-filter bypass vulnerability (**GHSA-42mf-vpmr-gw5r**).

**④ Data-interface security note.**

Official docs warn that Redis's `Serializer.PICKLE` hands code-execution capability to anyone who can write that stream.

The advice is to use only fully trusted Redis; JSON is the default.

**Unknown** — framework-level process / container sandbox defaults, not stated officially
(`agent_harness` and release pages checked).
axes.fit:
**Fits.**

- orchestrating **multi-agent conversations / protocolized networks** in Python (Hub + channel, with consulting, discussion, workflow adapters)
- needing auditable durable messaging (write-ahead log, audit trail) and cross-process deployment (WsLink)
- running on local models (Ollama / vLLM / LM Studio)
- wanting HITL and restricted shell tools
- needing MCP and AG-UI integration
- preferring opt-in, composable harness primitives

**Does not fit.**

- expecting `pip install ag2` to still be the old AutoGen API (since v1.0 the classic classes moved into `ag2-classic`)
- needing a vendor-hosted background (pure library, processes are your own)
- needing out-of-the-box container-level sandbox isolation (the official offering is a restricted-shell allowlist, not containers)
- non-Python stacks (no official non-Python port)

sections.一个必须讲清的版本断层：AG2 v1.0 把 Classic 拆出去了:
The README top uses a prominent notice:

> **Looking for `ConversableAgent`, `GroupChat`, or `import autogen`? That's now AG2 Classic.**

Since v1.0, the classic framework moved wholesale to the separate repository `ag2ai/ag2-classic`.

- classic line: `pip install ag2-classic`, `import autogen`, docs at `classic.docs.ag2.ai`
- new top-level package: `pip install ag2` is now the protocol-driven new framework

**The classic line is still maintained; existing code does not stop working.**

**The new top-level package no longer ships the `autogen` import name or the classic agent classes.**

The official wording on the upgrade path is blunt:

> AG2 v1.0 (`pip install ag2`) is **not** a drop-in upgrade from Classic.
> The agent model, orchestration, and imports all changed.

**So the answer to "is AG2 the new AutoGen" is: same lineage.**

**But v1.0 is not a lift-and-shift upgrade.**
sections.多 agent 编排：Network（Hub + channel）:
v1.0 uses **Network** to replace the classic `GroupChat` / swarm / nested chat:

> a `Hub` that owns the registry, the **write-ahead log**, and the **audit trail**,
> with agents talking over typed **channels**.

The official wording is explicit:

> "**This replaces the classic `GroupChat` / swarm / nested-chat patterns.**"

Four built-in channel adapters:

| Adapter | Participants | Speaking order | Termination |
|---|---|---|---|
| `conversation` | exactly 2 | free (either side at any time) | explicit close or TTL |
| `consulting` | exactly 2 | strict question-answer | auto-closes after the answer |
| `discussion` | 2+ | round-robin | explicit close or TTL |
| `workflow` | 2+ | declarative `TransitionGraph` | graph termination |

Of these, the official docs call `workflow` **"the closest counterpart to the classic GroupChat"**.

For deployment the default is `LocalLink` (same process). Switching to `WsLink` goes cross-process / cross-host with business code unchanged.
sections.harness：三组 opt-in 原语，正好落在「状态 ≠ 上下文」上:
Official `agent_harness` page wording:

> A bare `Agent` is just a model loop. The **harness** is the set of **opt-in primitives**
> you compose onto it.

| Parameter | Role | Corresponding dimension on this site |
|---|---|---|
| `assembly=` | context policy: `WorkingMemoryPolicy` / `SlidingWindowPolicy` / `AlertPolicy` | **context** |
| `knowledge=` | `KnowledgeStore` + `SummarizeCompact` / `TailWindowCompact` compaction + aggregation | **long-term memory + context compaction** |
| `tasks=` | subtask delegation (off by default), sub-Agent `tasks=False`, recursion impossible | **subagents** |

**This boundary is clean**: compaction (`compact=`) governs window usage.

The knowledge store (`KnowledgeStore`) governs cross-process persistent memory.
sections.权限：HITL + 受限 shell，但不是容器沙箱:
- **HITL**: `context.input(...)` inside a tool pauses the run to ask a human; `hitl_hook` decides the answer source.
- **Tool approval**: official v1.1.1 states approvals are keyed by "tool implementation", and only one same-named tool is exposed per turn.
- **Restricted shell**: `SandboxShellTool`'s `allowed=[...]` / `readonly=True` split the command into argv,
  then **check only the argv and execute verbatim**.

  Official wording:

  > "Nothing can expand after the check"

  The official docs also declare of `blocked=[...]`:

  > "best-effort. It is **not** a security boundary."

- v1.1.2 fixed a shell command-filter bypass vulnerability (**GHSA-42mf-vpmr-gw5r**),
  showing this class of tool's security surface needs watching across releases.

**Note: this is not container isolation** — the official offering is an allowlist and read-only mode.

**One more data-interface note.**

With `Serializer.PICKLE`, anyone who can write that Redis stream gains code-execution capability.

The official advice: use only fully trusted Redis; JSON is the default.
sections.核验说明:
Basis for `confidence: partial`:

**Why not verified**: this pass verified the v1.0-vs-Classic split, the Network Hub/channel abstraction,
the three harness primitive groups, the provider list (including local models).

The restricted shell and tool-approval mechanisms are also verified. The release cadence (v1.1.1 / v1.1.2) was verified this pass too.

But several items are **genuinely not given officially**:

- framework-level default file-access boundaries and container-level isolation
- hosting options and crash-resume semantics
- tool calling / structured output reliability after switching providers
- A2A implementation details in v1.0 (only seen in repository topics)

Plus fast version iteration (two releases within days), so it is not enough to raise to verified.

the `ag2ai/ag2-classic` repository.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs.

The test protocol is at [protocols/framework/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/framework/_protocol.md).

**Suggested measurement** (tailored to the orchestration-framework + multi-agent-conversation dimensions):

| # | What to test | Why it is worth testing |
|:--:|---|---|
| 1 | Effort to port a piece of classic GroupChat code using `WorkflowAdapter` | verifies the official "closest to GroupChat" claim |
| 2 | Switching `LocalLink` to `WsLink` cross-process deployment — does business code really stay unchanged | the official promise is the HubClient API stays the same |
| 3 | Usability of the restricted shell (`allowed`/`readonly`) under a realistic command set | stronger security often costs usability; the boundary needs measuring |
| 4 | Attach Ollama and run a multi-agent network, observing token and latency overhead | the real cost of local models + multi-agent |
| 5 | DiskKnowledgeStore + compaction across two runs, verifying cross-process memory really works | the README example claims it remembers after restart |
| 6 | The breaking-change surface of the two consecutive v1.1.x releases | fast iteration; selection needs quantified upgrade risk |

related: **Same-lineage divergence**: AG2 is the community continuation of AutoGen; MAF is Microsoft's official successor merging AutoGen with Semantic Kernel. The AutoGen sunset recorded by this site's harness section is why these two branches are collected separately.

**Abstraction-level contrast**: CrewAI uses the business metaphors of Crew (roles/goals/tasks) / Flow. AG2 v1.0 uses the protocolized abstraction of Network (Hub + typed channels). One leans toward team roles, the other toward message protocols and governance.

**Orchestration and HITL contrast**: ADK is a graph execution engine + tool-level confirmation. AG2 is a Hub/channel network + `context.input()` human review. Both provide state persistence, but at different granularity and semantics.
